units.translation: Do we seem to you to have been left behind in this battle?
may the gods never abandon the city during my lifetime

Here too M has λιχήν [lichen]. And so in other writers the manuscripts vary: see Thes. vol. 5 p. 174. The quantity of the first syllable is established from Nicander Ther. 945 ἵππειον λειχήνα [horse lichen].
lichens (thus Blomfield for λιχῆνας) eating away the ancient nature
γλῶσσα λείξασα [tongue having licked] Tyrwhitt for λέξασα [having spoken].
he licked his fill of tyrant's blood
or indeed you licked much of my blood
But we will raise a well-equipped chosen expedition
And the beds of men are filled with tears from longing
and the soft-robed couches of the beds
before ever to mount the bed
for maidens who have not tasted the marriage bed (thus Toupius for αστει μή)
where Toupius added δορᾶς [hide], comparing the glosses of Hesychius and Suidas λεόντειος δορά [lion's hide] and λεοντεία δορά [lion's hide].
and of the shaggy lion's hide
Where is the bronze-wrought vessel standing on lion's feet?
Should be written λεοντόχορτον [devoured by a lion] with L. Dindorf in Thes. vol. 5 p. 190.
a newly caught antelope devoured by a lion
λέπαδνον [yoke-strap] corrupted from λαπαδνόν [yoke-strap], which see.
he places the yoke-straps upon their necks
but when he entered the yoke-strap of necessity
the wing of a white hawk
τοῖς λεπτῶς κατεσκευασμένοις [to the finely constructed things].
I was awakened by the thin whirring of a gnat
from the fine-sanded mouths of the Nile (thus Pauwius for λεπτομαθῶν)
where now Λέρνης τε κρήνην [and the spring of Lerna] from the conjecture of Canterus.
to the deep meadow of Lerna

Should be written Λέσβιον φατνώματι [Lesbian in the panel] (or φατνώμασι [in the panels]) κῦμ᾽ ἐν τριγώνοις [wave in triangles], comparing Vitruvius 4, 6, 2 "sculpendum est cymatium Lesbium cum astragalo" [a Lesbian cymatium with astragal must be carved]; the interpreters and Schneider in his Lexicon understood this. (On the cyma or cymatium cf. R. Rochette Monum. inéd. vol. 1 p. 301.) The words of Pollux, unless they are more seriously corrupted by the scribes than that by deleting ἐκ before φατνώματα they can be restored, show that the grammarian did not understand the Aeschylean passage." L. Dindorf in Thes. vol. 5 p. 208.
And the Lesbian and the panel and the wave are parts of works in Aeschylus' Chamber-makers (fr. 72): "But let one man finish a Lesbian panel, a wave in triangles, with rhythms."
